record.interface_detail: a git push to a GitHub repository connected to a Vercel project runs every task tagged ci in turbo.json; a repository is enabled with the vercel ci enable command, runs and task logs are read in the dashboard CI tab, with the vercel ci CLI, the Vercel MCP and the REST API, and the status of the tasks is posted to the pull request as a check
record.tooling: Turborepo 2.11.7 or later and Vercel CLI 64.3.1 or later; tasks run in Linux containers on x86_64, Amazon Linux 2023 by default or Ubuntu 24.04 with a ci:os:ubuntu tag, with Node.js 24, git, Docker and common build tools preinstalled; extra tools are installed during bootstrapping with an install command in vercel.json
record.chaining: a hosted runner for tagged Turborepo tasks (lint, type check, tests, builds) triggered only by a git push to a private GitHub repository; it has no schedule, manual or pull-request trigger and no public-repository support, so GitHub Actions on a public repository and the other hosted runners of this topic come first for general jobs

record.provider: Vercel Deployment Storage / artifact store (Hobby, 30-day TTL)

free_tier.stated: 10 GB of Deployment Storage per Hobby team, and that pool is what every retained deployment output draws from. This is the clearest example in the whole slot of a 'free tier' that is a build-artifact store, not storage.

retention.stated: Deployment Retention defaults for Hobby are now 30 days for ALL four states. Canceled, errored, pre-production, production (Pro gets 180 days preview / 1 year production).

egress.terms: Served by Vercel's CDN at no separate charge while the deployment exists (Fast Data Transfer Hobby allowance is 100 GB, shared across all Vercel services). Deployment URLs are public unless Deployment Protection is on.

record.tooling: `vercel deploy` CLI / Git integration / REST Deployments API. No object-level API at all. You cannot address a file inside a deployment except by URL. No rclone backend and no possible wrapper, because there is no list/put primitive.
record.chaining: None useful. 10 GB is a hard pool shared by every project on the team, and going over it 'can block you from deploying until you free some up'. 200 projects on Hobby but one shared 10 GB. The multiplier actively works against you here.

limits.value: Retention defaults for Hobby are now 30 days
review deployments no longer get their own protection

record.limits_note: THE TTL IS THE STORY, and it tightened twice in 2026. Deployment Retention defaults for Hobby are now 30 days for ALL four states. Canceled, errored, pre-production, production (Pro gets 180 days preview / 1 year production). The Sept 16, 2026 changelog cut it further: 'Each Hobby project now keeps its 3 most recent production deployments, plus its 3 most recent deployments of any type, regardless of age. Preview deployments no longer get their own protection.' Deletion runs within 48 hours of eligibility, then a recovery window, then permanent removal. CLI source upload is capped at 100 MB per deploy (Hobby), 15,000 files.
record.reliability_note: Hard, automatic, irreversible expiry after 30 days. Any file hosted only in a deployment URL is gone a month later. Treat as a 30-day hot tier and nothing else.
